entries.keywords: family mother father brother sister grandmother grandfather relatives home
entries.a: A family is the people who love and care for you: mother, father, brothers, sisters, grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins. Families help each other and share.

entries.keywords: community helpers teacher nurse police farmer doctor jobs
entries.a: Community helpers keep us safe and healthy: the teacher educates, the nurse and doctor care for the sick, the police protect, the farmer grows food and the builder makes houses. Say thank you to them.

entries.keywords: seasons zimbabwe rainy season dry season winter summer climate weather
entries.a: Zimbabwe has a hot wet rainy season (roughly November to March), a cool dry winter (May to August) and a hot dry spell before the rains (September to October). Rain falls mostly in summer.

entries.keywords: minerals gold platinum diamonds coal chrome lithium mining resources zimbabwe
entries.a: Zimbabwe has many minerals, including gold, platinum, diamonds, coal, chrome and lithium. Mining brings income, but it must be done carefully to protect land and water.

entries.keywords: cities towns harare bulawayo mutare gweru masvingo kwekwe victoria falls
entries.a: Major places in Zimbabwe include Harare (the capital), Bulawayo, Mutare, Gweru, Masvingo, Kwekwe and Victoria Falls.

entries.keywords: neighbouring countries borders zambia mozambique south africa botswana landlocked
entries.a: Zimbabwe is landlocked (no coast). Its neighbours are Zambia (north), Mozambique (east), South Africa (south), and Botswana (west). Zimbabwe is in southern Africa.

entries.keywords: children's rights responsibilities education protection child abuse right to learn
entries.a: Every child has rights: to a name, to education, to health care, to play, to be safe and to be heard. Rights come with responsibilities, like respecting others, attending school and looking after property. If someone hurts you, tell a trusted adult or call Childline on 116.

entries.keywords: government parliament president executive legislature judiciary constitution citizen vote
entries.a: Government has three arms: the executive (President and ministers run the country), the legislature (Parliament makes laws) and the judiciary (courts apply the law). The Constitution is the highest law. Citizens aged 18 and over may vote.

entries.keywords: trade exports imports barter economy market demand supply
entries.a: Trade is buying and selling. Exports leave a country (tobacco, gold); imports come in. Barter swaps goods without money. When demand is high and supply is low, prices rise.

entries.keywords: history great zimbabwe munhumutapa rozvi khami trade gold kingdoms
entries.a: Before colonial rule, Zimbabwe had powerful states. Great Zimbabwe traded gold and ivory with coastal traders. Later came the Mutapa, Torwa/Khami and Rozvi states. Their stone ruins and trade show the skill of local people.

entries.keywords: chimurenga liberation struggle first second war independence 1980 history
entries.a: The First Chimurenga (1896-97) was resistance to colonial rule. The Second Chimurenga was the liberation struggle of the 1960s and 1970s, leading to independence on 18 April 1980. Heroes' Acre honours those who died.

entries.keywords: map skills compass directions north south east west scale key legend grid
entries.a: Map skills: the compass shows north, south, east and west. The key explains the symbols. The scale tells how real distances shrink on the map. Use grid references to find places.

entries.keywords: conserve water save water drought borehole dam rainwater harvesting
entries.a: Ways to save water: fix leaks, turn off taps, reuse washing water for plants, harvest rainwater, and keep rivers and wells clean. Boreholes and dams store water for dry times.

entries.keywords: maize mealie crop growing planting sadza staple farming rains
entries.a: Maize is Zimbabwe's main food crop; sadza is made from maize meal. Plant at the start of good rains, weed regularly, add manure or fertiliser and harvest when the cobs dry. Store dry grain safely away from pests.

entries.keywords: crops livestock cattle goats chickens tobacco cotton groundnuts sorghum millet farming
entries.a: Common crops are maize, sorghum, millet (small grains that cope with dry weather), groundnuts, cotton and tobacco. Common livestock are cattle, goats, sheep, pigs and chickens. Livestock give meat, milk, eggs, draught power and manure.

entries.keywords: vegetable garden school garden compost manure mulch spacing watering beds
entries.a: A good vegetable garden: pick a sunny spot near water, loosen and enrich the soil with compost or manure, plant at the right spacing, mulch to keep moisture, water in the morning or evening and remove weeds. Rotate crops each season.

entries.keywords: soil conservation contour ridges mulching crop rotation terracing erosion gully afforestation
entries.a: Soil conservation methods: contour ridges, mulching, terracing, crop rotation, planting grass and trees, and avoiding overgrazing. They stop erosion and keep soil fertile.

entries.keywords: compost making organic waste decompose heap fertiliser recycling
entries.a: To make compost: layer dry material (leaves, straw) with green material (vegetable waste, grass), add some soil, keep it damp and turn it. In a few weeks it becomes dark crumbly food for your plants. Do not add meat or plastic.
